target_customer: Biotech and pharmaceutical companies that pay for computationally designed or modeled antibodies
problem: Finding antibodies by wet lab screening is slow and trial and error, especially for hard targets. Macromoltek designs antibodies in silico using structural modeling and machine learning to cut experimental cycles.
business_model: Fee for service antibody design and modeling plus partnership models with biotech and pharma clients
product_category: Computational antibody design services and software

founders.name: Monica Berrondo
education: Ph.D. (institution not stated on the YC page or company site)
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC page and company site as a scientist and software engineer in antibody structure prediction with 10 plus peer reviewed articles.

founders.name: Susana Kaufmann
founders.background_notes: Company site describes her as a software and algorithm expert with over 25 years of experience who built the computational engine.

competitors.name: AbCellera
competitors.what: Machine learning assisted antibody discovery platform
competitors.traction_then: less than 1M raised before its first significant round per press
competitors.funding_then: 10M Series A led by DCVC Bio, September 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: De novo antibody design needs accurate structure prediction and design algorithms built by a very small team, with results needing wet lab validation by partners.

defensibility.rationale: A proprietary design engine and database built over years are hard to copy quickly, but results are not verified publicly and well funded competitors emerged later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent absorbing or copying it; well funded AI antibody firms (BigHat, Absci, Chai) emerged later and out raised it.

market_need_then: Pharma outsourced antibody discovery and biotech sought faster, cheaper discovery; Macromoltek reported working with large biopharmas and smaller biotechs, unnamed, and a 2017 contract research agreement with the ACC Bioscience Incubator.

branding.domain_note: macromoltek.com in use; no purchase detail found

identity.logo: Plain letter M per a directory listing; not verified
identity.visual_style: Science led, not described in detail on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and promotional: Revolutionizing Antibody Design, precision medicine

brand_strength.rationale: No evidence of brand awareness beyond a small B2B scientific audience; the name is a compound of macromolecule and tech that is hard to say.

outcome_analysis: Macromoltek is a small, founder led computational antibody design company with a team of 14 that sold design services after YC. No institutional funding was found in sources I could open, and the only funding hints (a 250K PPP loan in 2020 and totals of 370K or 1.5M) come from aggregators. It is still operating and stayed small while venture funded AI antibody companies such as BigHat and Absci raised much larger rounds, but the cause of its limited scale is not public.
notes: Funding: CB Insights alone reports 370K over four rounds including a 250K PPP loan in May 2020, and Bounce Watch reports 1.49M; neither is verified so no rounds are recorded. Founded year 2010 is the YC directory value seen in search results; a third party summary notes that the company site says fall 2010 and other sources say 2011. A search listing names a different person as CEO on one profile, unresolved. Outcome search returned no news of acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. No Y Combinator round amount is public. The ACC incubator page (August 2017) was opened and confirms a contract research agreement only.
